# Welcome {.unnumbered .unlisted}

This is the online version of **Leveraging AI Tools for
Academic Research: A One-Week Boot Camp**, by The rgtlab
Curriculum Project. We wrote it for faculty researchers who run
their own grant-funded projects, teach and supervise students,
and want AI tools to make that workload move faster without
making it riskier.

The primary payoff of this week is speed. A working
bibliography that once took hours now compiles in minutes. A
reproducible project skeleton that once took an afternoon now
scaffolds from a single prompt. A scattered set of notes
becomes a structured outline through a short dialog rather than
a blank page. We cover these efficiency techniques directly. We
also cover the verification and disclosure discipline that
keeps the speed from costing something worse: recognizing
hallucination and fabricated citations, reviewing AI-generated
code, protecting confidentiality, and disclosing AI use
honestly. A retraction, a misconduct finding, or a withdrawn
grant is expensive in a way that no week of saved time offsets.

That discipline matters, but it serves the efficiency rather
than the other way around. A faculty researcher takes this
workshop to get more done in a week with the same number of
hours. The risk material is worth reading because working fast
on someone else's terms (a journal's, a funder's, an IRB's) is
not fast at all if the work has to be redone. The book is
designed for **five consecutive days** of work: one hour of
lecture content each day, two hours of homework, and no
examinations.

The organizing principle is that AI tools are accelerants, not
replacements, for the judgment a researcher already exercises.
Each chapter opens with a concrete research task, develops the
AI-assisted technique that addresses it, and returns to the
task to judge what the technique did and did not solve,
including where it can mislead. An
[appendix](appendix-faculty.qmd) extends this discipline into
three roles specific to faculty life that the five-day
curriculum does not otherwise cover: writing grant proposals
under funder-specific AI rules, setting AI policy for one's own
students, and resolving AI-related authorship questions with
one's own trainees.

The workshop is a companion to the rgtlab curriculum
sequence:

- **R for Biostatistics: A One-Week Boot Camp**
  (<https://r-bootcamp.rgtlab.org>), the preparatory volume
  for R.
- [*Git and GitHub for
  Biostatistics*](https://git-bootcamp.rgtlab.org), the
  preparatory volume for version control.
- [*Biostatistics Practicum*](https://practicum.rgtlab.org),
  workflow infrastructure (Git in depth, Docker, renv,
  Quarto, CDISC), which this workshop draws on for
  reproducibility practice.
- [*Reproducible Research for the Health
  Sciences*](https://reproducibility.rgtlab.org), the
  reproducibility volume that this workshop's final chapter
  extends to cover AI provenance specifically.

A reader who has completed *R for Biostatistics* and *Git and
GitHub for Biostatistics* arrives at this workshop ready to
use AI tools inside an already-versioned, reproducible
research workflow.

See the [Preface](preface.qmd) for the design rationale
and the [Conventions](conventions.qmd) page for the visual
cues used throughout.
